scan_metadata.paper: Generative Predictive Control: Flow Matching Policies for Dynamic and Difficult-to-Demonstrate Tasks (Vince Kurtz, Joel Burdick; arXiv 2502.13406)
scan_metadata.scope_filter: Simulation training and headless evaluation of the shipped example tasks (pendulum, cart_pole, double_cart_pole, particle, pusht, walker, crane, humanoid); hardware and interactive viewing out of scope.
scan_metadata.filter_application: The filter is a scope description, not a path substring or title. It matches all eight examples/<task>.py and the library code they call; nothing outside that scope was selected. The README custom-robot path and the viewer-only functions were not selected.
scan_metadata.explanation: Static scan only: no repository code was run and nothing was imported or installed. Five tools in two modules are proposed. Every tool calls a function or method in the pinned gpc tree; one (gpc_rollout_policy_closed_loop) is the non-viewer code of gpc.testing.test_interactive extracted with its source attributed, so the coordinator should confirm it is in scope. The paper's Sec. VI-A comparison (average cost per step for GPC/GPC+/SPC/PPO over 100 randomized runs, warm starts vs inpainting) is not in the pinned commit; it exists only on the unmerged branches origin/rl and origin/evals and is deferred. Feasibility has not been measured. Heavy jobs are currently disabled, and every env constructor needs an offscreen OpenGL context.
scan_metadata.module_design_note: Modules group tools by workflow: gpc_training owns the tools built on gpc/training.py; gpc_inference owns the three tools that use a trained policy (gpc/policy.py, gpc/testing.py, gpc/sampling.py), whose usage the examples' test/sample branches document. This keeps assignments at two implementers and two verifiers on a memory-limited machine. A one-module-per-upstream-file split (gpc_policy, gpc_testing, gpc_sampling) is possible if the coordinator prefers it; tool names and source bindings stay the same.

tutorials.title: Pendulum swing-up example (train / test / sample)
tutorials.description: Trains a flow-matching policy for pendulum swing-up with gpc.training.train (PredictiveSampling 8 samples, 2 policy samples, 128 envs, 10 iterations); test opens an interactive viewer; sample bootstraps predictive sampling in hydrax's viewer.

suggested_tools.source_section: `if args.task == "train":` branch (lines 34-56) with env setup at line 31; calls gpc.training.train (gpc/training.py:236-500)
suggested_tools.description: Train a GPC flow-matching policy on a shipped example task with the example's settings; returns the saved policy, checkpoints and per-iteration training curves.
suggested_tools.primary_input: task name (one of the eight examples) plus optional problem-size overrides and an output directory
suggested_tools.outputs: policy .pkl, checkpoints, TensorBoard log, per-iteration policy cost / SPC cost / fraction policy-best / loss / timings
suggested_tools.applicable_to_new_data: Yes for new problem sizes and hyperparameters on the shipped tasks; new robots need a user-defined Hydrax task (out of scope).

tutorials.reference_execution: pendulum preset with num_iters=2, num_envs=32 (upstream 10, 128); keep episode_length=200, SPC 8/0.1, num_policy_samples=2, num_epochs=10, batch_size=128; num_videos=2 is cheap if GL works, else 0 (record). If killed at the cap, num_envs=16.

tutorials.title: Training, simulation, fitting and policy tests
tutorials.description: pytest tests test_simulate (simulate_episode shapes on ParticleEnv), test_fit (fit_policy on synthetic bimodal data), test_train (3-iteration particle training + direction check of the trained policy) and test_policy (Policy apply/save/load).

suggested_tools.source_section: test_simulate (lines 21-59); implementation gpc/training.py::simulate_episode (lines 21-125), vmapped as in train's jit_simulate (lines 363-381)
suggested_tools.description: Evaluate a GPC policy headlessly on new random initial states with policy-augmented SPC; report per-step best SPC vs best policy sample costs and the fraction of states where the policy sample was best.
suggested_tools.primary_input: task name, policy .pkl (or an untrained policy), num_envs, seed, strategy ('policy' or 'best')
suggested_tools.outputs: mean J_spc, mean J_policy, fraction policy-best, per-env/per-step cost arrays, observation/action-sequence (and optional state) trajectories .npz
suggested_tools.applicable_to_new_data: Yes: new policies/checkpoints, seeds, numbers of initial states and deployment strategies.

tutorials.reference_execution: Run tests/test_training.py unchanged (test_simulate tiny; test_fit 1000 steps on 192 points; test_train particle 128 envs x 100 steps x 16 samples x 3 iters with num_videos=2). Run from a scratch working directory (the tests create _test_train/ and _test_policy/ relative to the cwd) so the repository is not modified. Test sizes cannot be reduced without editing the tests; if test_train exceeds the cap, record that and run the same calls through a driver with num_envs=32 as a labelled deviation.

supporting_for.gpc_sample_policy_actions: test_policy (lines 177-234) and the direction check in test_train (lines 162-170)

tutorials.title: Cart-pole swing-up example (train / test / sample)
tutorials.description: Trains a cart-pole flow-matching policy, then either runs it with warm starts in an interactive viewer (test) or uses it to bootstrap predictive sampling in hydrax's viewer (sample).

suggested_tools.description: Sample action sequences from a trained GPC policy for a given observation with warm-start level alpha and flow step dt.
suggested_tools.primary_input: policy .pkl, observation vector, optional previous action sequence, warm_start_level, inference_timestep, num_samples, seed
suggested_tools.outputs: num_samples x horizon x nu action sequences in physical units
suggested_tools.applicable_to_new_data: Yes: any observation of the policy's task.

suggested_tools.source_section: `test` branch (lines 57-61) -> gpc.testing.test_interactive loop (gpc/testing.py:30-85) without viewer, sleep and print; bounded by num_steps
suggested_tools.description: Headless closed-loop GPC simulation with per-step re-planning and warm starts; returns state/control/observation trajectories and inference times.
suggested_tools.primary_input: task name, policy .pkl, num_steps, warm_start_level, inference_timestep, seed, optional initial state
suggested_tools.outputs: qpos/qvel/ctrl/observation time series and per-step inference time (.npz + summary)
suggested_tools.applicable_to_new_data: Yes: new initial states, warm-start levels and policies.

suggested_tools.source_section: `sample` branch (lines 63-76) -> gpc.sampling.BootstrappedPredictiveSampling.__init__/optimize (gpc/sampling.py:12-90); one headless optimize call instead of hydrax run_interactive
suggested_tools.description: GPC+ planning step: predictive sampling bootstrapped with policy samples from a given state; returns the optimized action sequence and costs of Gaussian vs policy samples.
suggested_tools.primary_input: task name, policy .pkl, state (default MjData), num_samples, num_policy_samples, noise_level, warm_start_level, inference_timestep, seed
suggested_tools.outputs: optimized action-sequence knots, per-rollout costs split by sample source, best cost per source, policy-sample-best flag
suggested_tools.applicable_to_new_data: Yes: new states, policies and sample budgets.

tutorials.reference_execution: cart_pole preset train with num_iters=2, num_envs=16, num_epochs=10 (upstream 10, 128, 100) to obtain a policy; then Policy.apply with the test settings (dt 0.1, alpha 1.0), a headless closed loop of about 200 MuJoCo steps from the default MjData, and one BootstrappedPredictiveSampling.optimize call with the sample settings (2 policy + 1 Gaussian samples, noise 0.1).
